subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of tangent and normal to the ellipse x² + 8y² − 33 = 0 at (−1, 2).

insider_note: The tangent uses the S₁ = 0 rule directly on the given equation — there is no need to first divide into x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 form for this one.

steps.label: Equation of the tangent
steps.margin_note: First two marks. Replace x² by x·x₁ and y² by y·y₁ — the S₁ = 0 rule.
steps.memory_tip: S₁ = 0 means: replace each squared variable by (variable)×(its value at the given point).
lines: Equation of the ellipse: S = x² + 8y² − 33 = 0
Equation of the tangent at (−1, 2) is S₁ = 0:
steps.why: For a conic S = 0, the tangent at a point (x₁, y₁) on it is found by the S₁ = 0 substitution rule — replacing x² with x·x₁ and y² with y·y₁ — without needing the ellipse in x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 form first.
common_mistakes: Substituting x₁ = −1, y₁ = 2 into x² and y² instead of into x·x₁ and y·y₁.
Losing the negative sign from x₁ = −1 when multiplying it by x.

steps.label: Equation of the normal
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. The normal is perpendicular to the tangent at the same point.
steps.memory_tip: Find the tangent's slope first, then flip and negate it for the normal.
steps.why: The normal to a curve at a point is the line through that point perpendicular to the tangent there, so its slope is the negative reciprocal of the tangent's slope.
common_mistakes: Using the same slope as the tangent instead of its negative reciprocal.
Sign errors when expanding −16(x + 1) — it becomes −16x − 16, not −16x + 16.
